Inference, tool execution, and HTTP transport are left to the caller.
Comparison competitors (K3, GLM-5.3, GPT-5.6 Sol, Opus 5) and all figures come from DeepSeek's own card; no independent evaluation or methodology detail is provided.
summary: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is a minor revision of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash released under the MIT License, with the stated focus of KV cache compression and reduced output length to improve cost and latency on agentic workloads. DeepSeek's own benchmark table reports gains over the prior Flash and over K3 and GLM-5.3 across Terminal-Bench 4.0 (42.3), DeepSWE v1.1 (77.0), Apex Bench v1.1 (72.1), Automation-Bench v1.0.6 (60.5), and Agents' Last Exam (35.4), while trailing Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol on several text and reasoning tasks such as HLE and ProgramBench. All numbers are vendor self-reported; only harness names (Claude Code for Terminal-Bench, Mini-SWE-V2 for DeepSWE) are given, with no further methodology. The model supports a 1M-token context with recommended max_tokens >= 256K and temperature/top_p of 1.0. It ships without a Jinja chat template, instead providing a Python reference encoding (encoding.py) and deepseek-recipe, Rust libraries with Python bindings that translate Messages, Chat Completions, and Responses API requests into V4/V4.1 prompts and parse output including thinking, tool calls, images, and streaming, while leaving inference, tool execution, and HTTP transport to the caller.

title: GitLab warns of max severity code execution vulnerability

notes: CVE-2026-97229, rated maximum severity: an integer overflow in GitLab's CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler, which parses, compiles, and evaluates regexes in pipeline configuration files.

Article gives no public exploit, no in-the-wild exploitation for this CVE, and no detail on the 'certain conditions' required to trigger it.
summary: GitLab issued a Monday advisory urging immediate patching of CVE-2026-97229, a maximum-severity flaw in its CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler. The vulnerability is an integer overflow caused by insufficient validation of regular expressions in pipeline configuration files; GitLab states it could, under certain conditions, allow an unauthenticated user to run arbitrary code on the server via a specially crafted regex. It was reported by a researcher using the handle 'joaxcar' through GitLab's HackerOne program. Fixes shipped in CE/EE 19.2.8, 19.3.4, and 19.4.2; GitLab.com is already patched and Dedicated customers are unaffected, while self-managed installations must upgrade. The article notes CISA has flagged five GitLab flaws exploited since 2021 (one by ransomware gangs) and cites GitLab's claims of 30M+ users and adoption by over half the Fortune 100, but provides no evidence of in-the-wild exploitation of this specific CVE and no detail on the triggering conditions.

title: The State of Context Engineering
why: The fix for a misbehaving long-running agent is usually to delete context, not swap models: the author's practical warning line is ~200K tokens, and the same six-move toolbox still handles the newest "agents that drive their own harness" failures.
notes: Four long-context failure modes: poisoning (a bad fact lodges and won't clear, e.g. Gemini 2.5 playing Pokemon Red kept trying to bribe a guard with iced tea from FireRed's weights instead of the correct lemonade), distraction (long context overrides base knowledge), confusion (irrelevant facts skew answers), and clash (tools/skills/memory conflict).

Context distraction is quantified via 'Do as I Say, Not as I Do' (Camassa and Shiller): with an instruction to answer in Russian plus contradictory French examples, Gemma 3 12B obeys less than half the time after a few bad examples; Opus 4.6 resists longer but still breaks. Gemini 2.5's technical report appendix notes that past ~100K tokens the agent repeated past actions instead of planning.

Six fixes, all older than the problems and increasingly moved from model calls into the harness/code: context augmentation (RAG, skills), tool loadout (filter exposed tools; one enterprise loaded 600 skills per engineer at startup), quarantine (subagents with blank history), pruning (Claude Code/Codex strip stale tool results during compaction), offloading (store state in files/DB), and summarization (compaction). Demoed as ~16 lines of DSPy changes.

Two new failure modes from harness-trained agentic models: 'fighting the weights' (models overfit to training tools, so e.g. Claude Code's prompt repeats 'make parallel tool calls' up to seven times to override serial-trained habits; smaller models botch Playwright MCP calls on first try), and 'context inertia' (models fixate on one hypothesis and won't stop).

Context inertia reported by four parties in one week; shared fix is periodic forgetting while preserving the environment: Anthropic's Memento harness clears context every ~1.5 hours after writing a note; Microsoft Research's 'Fork-and-Flush'; UC Berkeley's 'Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting' (Shangyin Tan) shows a performance jump at each context clear.

Framing is a talk transcript from AGNTCon tied to the author's forthcoming O'Reilly book The Context Engineering Handbook; cited agent-horizon numbers (METR-style) are GPT-5 ~3.4h, Gemini 3.1 ~6.4h, Opus 4.6 ~12h, with harness. Note the piece is dated 2026 and references unreleased/speculative models (Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1, personal agents like Hermes), so treat model names and numbers as the author's claims, not verified benchmarks.
